top_problem: There is no page-wide baseline grid. Each card sets its own 12 pt grid from its figure height, so row-1 items are 5.25 pt out of step across cards and the body rules stagger in both rows. The lotería concept also stops at generic flat icons: the boldest missing idea is to make the page a true lotería tabla, with a card-anatomy module every card snaps to and each card carrying a gritón verse (the caller's rhyme) in place of the plain English header.
fixes: Lock every card body to one page-wide 12 pt baseline anchored at the deck top (131.99). Fix figure heights in whole 12 pt steps so that the body rule, first item and name bar sit at the same y in every card of a row, including card 1's 11.5 pt featured items.
Use one fixed figure box per row so the body rules line up across all three cards, and bottom-align content to the name bar rather than letting figures flex to fill space.
Pick one card-title treatment, either all centred on the card axis or all set a fixed distance from the ordinal. Currently titles run from x 73.73 to 481.14 with mixed logic.
Merge the one-item Brandy and Classics cards into fuller cards, or give them a second, lotería-style verse or description line, so that 55-69% of the card is not filler figure.
Put the Agave subhead on the same mod-12 phase as the Draft, Glass and Sparkling subheads, and give card 1 the standard 6 pt item gap (it is 5.25 pt now) so the featured card follows the same rhythm.

top_problem: Each card has three competing header layers, and the measurements break two of them. The loudest element, the coloured Spanish lotería name bar, sits at the foot where it reads as a button or footer. The English card title (11.5 pt, and 13 pt on the featured card) is visually the weakest and is centred in whatever width is left beside the ordinal, so it floats at a different optical position on every card (x = 73.7, 277.7, 472.9, 97.9, 302.6, 481.1). Criterion 2 is a measured fail on two counts. First, the same level has two styles: the featured card's title is 13 pt with h 15.75 at y 146.48, while the others are 11.5 pt with h 14.25 at y 147.98. Second, subheader spacing is inconsistent: 15.0 pt above the first subheader (DRAFT, BY THE GLASS) but 9.0 pt above the mid-card ones (CIDER, SPARKLING, AGAVE), with 0 pt below every subheader. The gap above the name bar is also 8.74 pt on Beer/Wine but 7.24 pt on Brandy. The missing big idea: make the lotería name bar the header itself. The real lotería puts number plus Spanish name as one unit, so a true card needs a single bilingual top-or-bottom title system, not an English title at the top and a Spanish title at the bottom.
fixes: Pick one header level per card: move the Spanish lotería name (EL AGAVE, LA COPA...) into the foot bar as the one card title with the English name as a small italic line under it, and delete the top English header, or the reverse, so each card has one title level, not two competing ones.

Use one header style on all six cards: the featured card's title must match the others' 11.5 pt and y 147.98 (show the feature through the terracotta frame and tint only), and left-align every title at ordinal x + fixed offset (e.g. 22 pt) instead of centring it in the leftover width.

Give every subheader (AGAVE, DRAFT, CIDER, BY THE GLASS, SPARKLING) the same space above it (e.g. 9 pt, or 12 pt on the baseline) and a fixed 2-3 pt below it: today the first subheader gets 15 pt above and the mid-card ones 9 pt, with 0 pt below all of them.

Make the gap above the name bar the same on every card (Brandy is 7.24 pt, the others 8.74 pt): pin the bar to the card's bottom padding and let the figure flex, and put the same rule-to-body gap under the divider on every card.

Balance the subheader system: card 1 labels AGAVE under the Margarita but gives the Margarita no subheader, and the Classics and Brandy cards have none, while proposal.md claims pairs (De la casa, Clásicos, Brandy y coñac) that are not printed. Either give every card body a bilingual subheader or keep them only where a card holds two groups.

lens: palette, contrast, price and number styling

measurements.price_right_pt_per_card: one right edge per card (220.5, 392.5, 564.49), pass; all prices bare integers with no $, consistent
measurements.palette_count: 4 accents (terracotta, agave, marigold, rosa) plus cream, ink and muted, which is the scorecard's upper limit

top_problem: The lotería idea stays on the surface. These are framed boxes with clip-art icons, not real lotería cards: there is no cantor verse, no card-number system that runs through to the prices, and no tabla. On top of that, the rosa accent is a fifth voice that shows up only in the ordinals and a few figure specks. It never appears in the papel picado, so the numbers look borrowed from another palette, and the ordinals compete with the terracotta prices for the eye. The boldest missing idea is each card carrying its cantor's riddle-verse, so the menu is played rather than just labelled.
fixes: Either work lotería rosa into the papel picado and the name bars so it belongs to the system, or drop it and set the ordinals in terracotta or ink; right now the rosa ordinals (4.66:1 on the featured card) shout louder than the prices.
Add one line of the cantor's verse per card, in Fraunces italic in the muted colour, under the card name (for example 'La Copa' with its call), so the concept is enacted and not just decorated.

Make the header row consistent: set every card name either centred on the card axis or on a fixed left edge after the ordinal; at the moment 'Margarita & Agave' and 'House Originals' sit off-centre while 'Classics', 'Brandy' and 'Wine' are centred.

Rebalance the thin cards: Brandy's figure takes 69% of its card and Classics 55%, each over a single item, so shrink those figures or merge Brandy into the Agave/spirits card, and give the reclaimed height to the item-dense cards.

Give prices their own quiet emphasis: drop the price to Fraunces 500 at 10 pt, or add a hairline leader, so terracotta prices at the same size and weight as item names stop sitting level with the names in the hierarchy; also use a terracotta frame for the featured card only, keeping the ink double frame for the rest, and document that as a rule.

lens: design concept and elevating elements vs the best bar menus in the country

measurements.price_format: whole numbers, no $, the same on every card

measurements.header_x_per_column_pt: col 1: 73.73 vs 97.91; col 2: 277.71 vs 302.64; col 3: 472.85 vs 481.14. The names are centred in the space to the right of the ordinal, not on the card, so they sit visibly off-centre (Classics, Brandy, Wine)

top_problem: The lotería idea is a label, not a system. These are six framed boxes of text with generic flat bar icons (rocks glass, coupe, barrel, bottle). The figures are not lotería-style illustrations, and each card has two titles (English header on top, Spanish name bar at the foot). Card size ignores content, so a name-only $18 Cognac gets a full card that is 69% illustration while four beers are packed together. The boldest missing idea: make each card a real lotería card, drawn in one hand-cut, woodblock-like illustration style, with the Spanish lotería name (EL AGAVE, LA COPA) as the only card title and the text list set as the card's 'reverse' or in a tabla grid, so the page reads as a playable tabla rather than a boxed list.
fixes: Give every card-name header one size and set it centred on the card's full width (or all flush-left after the ordinal), so row 1 and row 2 headers share one y and one alignment; this clears the measured criterion 2 failure.

Size cards by content instead of by an equal grid: fold Brandy into the agave/spirits card or turn it into a half-height card, and give the freed space to cocktails, so no single name-only item sits under a 69% illustration.

Replace the generic flat bar icons with one illustration language that belongs to lotería (heavy outline, woodcut or hand-cut paper texture, off-register colour), and add at least one figure the venue can own, such as a cantina character or an Iowa City reference.

Drop either the English header or the Spanish name bar as the card title (keep the lotería name as the title and set the English as a small italic gloss), and cut the doubled English/Spanish subheads so each card has one clear title level.

Replace the stock papel picado strip and the generic 'Cantina & Cocktail Bar' masthead with a tabla-style frame or a card-back pattern, and pull the section order together (cocktails, then spirits including brandy, then beer, then wine) so Brandy no longer splits Beer from Wine.
note: Not reviewed: preview-phone.png, doc.json, menu.html, menu.pdf. Criterion 10 is scored from the letter preview only; the phone layout is not checked.

top_problem: On a phone the lotería idea turns into a long scroll of six same-looking framed cards. Two of them (Classics, Brandy) spend a full screen of frame, figure and name bar on a single line, and the tab bar shows unlabeled icons. The boldest missing idea is the tabla: the phone should open as a lotería tabla, a 3x2 board of the six cards with frijol markers. Tapping a card would 'deal' it open, turning the navigation itself into the game, where now it is a strip of pennants. Measured: print margins 36/36/36/36 pt, 12 pt gutters, one price right edge per card (220.5/392.5/564.49), 6 pt item gaps. Those are the price of entry. The phone's 0.7-0.8 degree tilt shifts the price column and rules by about 5 css px across the card width, so the phone copy leaves the grid that print holds.
fixes: Make the phone navigation a real lotería tabla (3x2 grid of mini cards with the Spanish name bars, with a frijol marker on the active card) that replaces the unlabeled pennant tabs. Each tab currently shows only a numeral and a roughly 20 px icon; only the active one gets a label, and that label ('Agave') matches neither the card title ('Margarita & Agave') nor the bar ('EL AGAVE').

Pick one name per section and use it everywhere: tab, card title and name bar. Card 1 now carries three names ('Agave' / 'Margarita & Agave' / 'EL AGAVE') and also an 'AGAVE Del agave' subheader inside it.

Merge Classics into House Originals as one 'Cocteles' card, and fold Brandy into the agave/spirits card. That removes the two one-item cards whose figures fill 55% and 69% of the card height. The page then reads cocktails → beer → wine → spirits, and on the phone it stops spending a full screen per single line.

Keep the dealt-card tilt on the card frame and shadow only, and counter-rotate or un-rotate the inner text block, so baselines, the item rules and the price column stay truly horizontal and vertical on the phone as they do in print.

Set the phone figures to one fixed scale (for example 35% of the card width). Right now the agave nearly fills the width while the copita and bottle drop to icon size, so the phone cards look like different menus from each other and from the print deck.

lens: every item and price vs the draft (build/draft_doc.json) for round-6
top_problem: All 14 items and prices match the draft: nothing added, dropped or re-priced. The content under the prices is lopsided, though. The four cocktails get full recipe copy, but Añejo Tequila and Cognac VSOP print with no description at all. Blanco Tequila's only line is 'Also called plata.', which is not a description. The three beers have no ABV and the three wines have no region. Everything missing is flagged, so nothing is invented, but the menu still fails criterion 8's standard of 'every item has a description with its ingredients'. The section flow makes this worse: Cognac VSOP alone fills a whole card called 'Brandy', placed between Beer and Wine. That gives the thinnest item on the menu a full panel, while the tequilas are tucked inside the Margarita card. Wine sits under a 'LA BOTELLA' (the bottle) banner even though every wine price is by the glass or has no label.
fixes: Give Añejo Tequila and Cognac VSOP a printed line built from the draft's own facts (e.g. 'Aged tequila, served neat' / 'VSOP Cognac, served neat'). Replace 'Also called plata.' with a real description of Blanco Tequila, and keep brand, age and pour size flagged in missing_ingredients.

Put spirits in one place: move Cognac VSOP out of its own card into a combined 'Spirits' card with Blanco and Añejo, or make Card 1 cocktails-only. Then reorder to cocktails, then beer and cider, then wine, then spirits, so no single item gets a full card.

Rename the wine card's 'LA BOTELLA' banner (e.g. 'EL VINO' or 'POR COPA'). Also label Brut Rosé's price as glass or bottle once the venue answers, so the banner does not contradict the 'By the glass / Por copa' subheader.

Remove the repeated agave labels in Card 1: 'Margarita & Agave' heading, 'AGAVE / Del agave' subheader and 'EL AGAVE' banner. Keep one, so the spirits subsection reads as its own category and not as more cocktails.

Before print, ask the venue through the Coordinator for beer ABV and style, wine region, and the spirit age statement. Criterion 8 cannot go above the mid-50s while every non-cocktail line lacks the required fact for its category.

top_problem: Description depth is lopsided: the four cocktails get full spirit, modifiers, garnish, method and glass lines, but Añejo Tequila and Cognac VSOP print no description at all (round 6 dropped the draft's 'Añejo tequila pour.' and 'VSOP Cognac pour.'). Blanco gets only 'Also called plata.', and beer, cider and wine keep three-word placeholders with no ABV, style detail or region. Half the menu reads as unfinished.
fixes: Restore a description under Añejo Tequila and Cognac VSOP using only known facts (at minimum the draft's 'Añejo tequila pour.' / 'VSOP Cognac pour.', or type and age class such as 'Aged tequila' and 'VSOP-grade Cognac'), and keep brand, pour and age flagged instead of leaving blank lines under a name.

Change 'Also called plata.' into a real type description (for example 'Blanco (plata) tequila, 100% agave' only if sourced; otherwise 'Blanco tequila, also called plata'), so the line names the spirit and does not read like a footnote.

Escalate the open wine, beer and cider flags (region for Malbec, Pinot Grigio and Brut Rosé; ABV and brewery for the three drafts and the cider) to the Coordinator as blocking. Until they are answered, write each line as grape or style plus a sourced tasting cue so these sections are not visibly thinner than the cocktails.

Rebalance the section flow: Brandy (one item, 69% figure) sits between Beer and Wine and splits the spirits across cards 1 and 5, and Classics is left with one item. Merge Brandy into a spirits card or pair it with Classics, so reading order runs cocktails, then spirits, then beer and cider, then wine, and every category gets equal weight.

Resolve the two content risks before print: label the Brut Rosé price as glass or bottle (it is unlabelled now), and get a venue answer on the Old Fashioned dairy allergen and on the Manhattan omitting bitters, which the draft description printed.

lens: flow and section order for a Mexican restaurant and cocktail bar in Iowa City
top_problem: Section flow breaks down on the second row. After the three cocktail cards it runs Beer & Cider, then Brandy, then Wine, so a single spirit sits between beer and wine. The agave spirits are on card 1 but Cognac has its own card. Two one-item cards, Classics (Manhattan) and Brandy (Cognac VSOP, where the figure takes 69% of the card), take up a third of the page. This is where a cantina should be selling its highest-margin items, and here the reader has to hunt. All 14 items and prices match the draft exactly, and nothing was dropped or invented. Margarita moved from Classics to the Agave card, which the proposal notes.
problems: Order is cocktails, beer, brandy, wine: spirits come before wine and are split across two places (Agave on card 1, Brandy on card 5), which goes against the scorecard's cocktails, beer, wine, spirits flow
Two one-item cards (Classics and Brandy) waste prime page area on figures, while the six-item cards feel full and the one-item cards look empty
Añejo Tequila and Cognac VSOP are printed with no description at all, and Blanco's 'Also called plata.' is only a synonym, not a description (these gaps are flagged, not invented)
Beer has no ABV and wine has no region or grape detail beyond the draft words ('Dry red wine.' for Malbec); these are flagged, but criterion 8 is not met

Brut Rosé price has no glass or bottle label, and there is no pour-size label on any spirit or wine price. The format is consistent (no $, whole numbers), but the missing serve context weakens criterion 3
fixes: Reorder the deck to cocktails (Agave/Margarita, House Originals, Classics), then Beer & Cider, then Wine, then one Spirits card (Mezcal/Tequila plus Brandy) at the end so spirits are no longer split.
Merge Classics into the House Originals card (or the Margarita card) and merge Brandy into an Agave & Spirits card, so no card holds a single item and the freed space goes to the cocktails.

Write short descriptions for Añejo and Cognac VSOP, and extend Blanco's line, using only sourced facts (type or age class, for example 'aged tequila' or 'VSOP-grade cognac', if a category row supports it); otherwise print a visible 'ask your server' line and keep the flag.
Get ABV for the beers and region for the wines from the venue through the Coordinator, and hold approval of criterion 8 until they are printed.
Resolve the Brut Rosé glass or bottle question and add a 'glass' label (or a Por copa header note) covering every wine price, so the reader does not have to guess the serve.

top_problem: The copy has no single voice, and the depth of description changes a lot from card to card. The Margarita gets ingredients, then a tasting note, then the method. The Old Fashioned, Daiquiri and Manhattan get spec-sheet shorthand ('Stirred; up, in a coupe.') with no tasting note. Blanco gets a trivia line ('Also called plata.'). Añejo and Cognac VSOP print with no description. Beer and wine lines are generic ('Dry red wine.', 'Hop-forward draft IPA.' mostly repeats the name). Card 1 reads like a menu and cards 5 and 6 read like an inventory. The language system also splits three ways: English card titles, Spanish name bars, and bilingual eyebrows on only 3 of 6 cards. The proposal lists De la casa, Clásicos and Brandy y coñac, but none of them is printed. Prices are consistent integers and all 14 items and prices match build/draft_doc.json exactly: nothing was added, changed or dropped. Unknowns are flagged in proposal.md: pour sizes, ABV, region and producer, Añejo age, Cognac house, Rosé glass or bottle.
fixes: Give every cocktail the same three-part structure in the same order (spirit and modifiers; garnish; one short tasting note taken from draft or recipe words), and write the method as a full phrase ('stirred and served up in a coupe') instead of semicolon shorthand. If there is no sourced tasting note, drop the Margarita's so all four match.

Fix the order and spirits split: move Brandy after Wine (Agave, Originals, Classics, Beer and Cider, Wine, Spirits), or put Cognac VSOP on one Spirits card with Blanco and Añejo, so spirits sit in one place and not between beer and wine.

Use one bilingual system on all six cards: either print the Spanish subtitle (De la casa, Clásicos, Brandy y coñac) under every English title, or remove the bilingual eyebrows. Also remove the 'AGAVE / Del agave' eyebrow, which repeats the card 1 title.

Block the Añejo, Cognac VSOP, beer ABV and wine region lines as 'pending venue input' in doc.json and get the answers through the Coordinator before print. Until then, replace 'Also called plata.' with a line in the same guest voice as the others, or leave Blanco name-only like Añejo, so the tequila pair matches.
Put a clear 'glass' or 'bottle' label on the Brut Rosé price once the venue answers, and show pour sizes next to spirit and draft beer prices so the price column reads the same in every card.

lens: how missing data is handled and flagged
top_problem: All the missing data is flagged in meta and proposal.md, but none of it is resolved or shown on the menu. Anejo Tequila ($16) and Cognac VSOP ($18), the two most expensive spirit pours, print as bare names with no description. Beer has no ABV, wine has no region, and Brut Rose ($13) has no glass or bottle label and sits under 'Sparkling' next to the by-the-glass wines, so a guest will read it as a glass price. Prices all match the draft and nothing is invented. The flagging is honest, but the guest gets a menu with visible holes.
fixes: Add a factual type line for Anejo and Cognac VSOP from the draft or the beverage_categories rows (for example the category's own aging wording, if a row supplies it) and keep brand, age and pour flagged, so no premium pour prints as a name only.
Mark Brut Rose's price as 'glass' or 'bottle' only once the venue answers; until then, move it out of the implied by-the-glass run or hold it back, so it is not misread as a glass price.

Put the spirits back together and fix the section flow: Brandy (card 5) currently sits between Beer and Wine, and the Margarita was moved out of the draft's Classics into the Agave card, leaving Classics and Brandy as one-item cards with empty-looking figure space. Either put the Margarita back in Classics or record the regrouping as a venue question.
Replace 'Also called plata.' with a real spirit description once the brand or type facts arrive. A synonym is not a description, so Blanco should count as flagged, not as described.

Make the Coordinator's needs_input a short, ranked list the venue can answer in one reply (ABV and brewery for 3 beers and the cider; producer and region for 3 wines; Anejo and VSOP brand and age; Brut Rose format; Manhattan bitters; dairy allergen), so round 7 can print these facts rather than flag them again.

lens: trace printed ingredients, garnishes, glass and serve to sources
top_problem: All glassware, garnish and method lines check out against phg.recipe_versions. But 'fresh lime' is printed on the Margarita and the House Daiquiri, and neither recipe row supports 'fresh'. The only 'fresh' in the data is 'fresh ice' in the Margarita method (rv f06abb74), and the Daiquiri method (rv 14d45e57) is 'Shake with ice and fine strain'. 'Agave syrup' and 'demerara syrup' add 'syrup' to draft words that say only 'agave' and 'demerara', and recipe_components is empty for all four cocktails, so nothing supports it. Beyond that, 8 of the 14 lines are either stub draft copy ('Dry red wine.', 'Crisp pale lager.') or missing entirely (Añejo, Cognac VSOP), so half the menu reads like an inventory list, not a cantina.
verified: Margarita (menu_items 14555870): glass Rocks, garnish Lime wheel, method 'Shake with ice and strain over fresh ice' (recipe_versions f06abb74) support 'lime wheel', 'Shaken; on the rocks'. Draft supports 'Tequila blanco, lime, orange liqueur, agave. Bright and citrus-forward.' Not supported: 'fresh' lime, agave 'syrup'.

Brown Butter Old Fashioned (0cc4e912): rv 7095fd3d gives Rocks, Orange peel, 'Stir with ice and strain over a large cube', which supports 'orange peel. Stirred; over a large cube'. Draft 'Brown butter-washed bourbon, demerara, bitters.' Not supported: demerara 'syrup'.

House Daiquiri (44dcba6e): rv 14d45e57 gives Coupe, Lime coin, 'Shake with ice and fine strain', which supports 'lime coin. Shaken; up, in a coupe'. Draft 'White rum, lime, and house demerara syrup.' Not supported: 'fresh' lime.

Manhattan (bf732e78): rv 9fb77eaa gives Coupe, Cocktail cherry, 'Stir with ice and strain', which supports the printed serve. The draft menu_description does include 'aromatic bitters'. The menu leaves it off on the strength of a public_components flag that the designer cites but that I did not check. 'Rye whiskey' is an acceptable reading of 'Rye'.
Beer, cider and wine lines (90b0a7e3, 8fb136cd, 70657e1e, 65c39a14, f6f9d57e, 5ba7511f, 32a35bd3) match the draft menu_description word for word.
Blanco Tequila 'Also called plata.' traces only to the beverage_categories 04d72e1f name, as the designer cites it. Draft line is 'Blanco tequila pour.'
All 14 printed items and prices match the draft. The retired Junmai Ginjo (57617f46) is correctly left off.
problems: Criterion 11: 'fresh lime' (x2) and 'agave syrup' / 'demerara syrup' are embellishments with no source. recipe_components returns null for all four cocktail recipe versions, and the proposal's claim that 'fresh' and 'syrup' come from the recipe is false for the lime and only half-true for the ice.

Criterion 12: 'Dry red wine.', 'Dry white wine.', 'Crisp pale lager.', 'Dry sparkling cider.' and 'Also called plata.' are category glosses, not guest language. Añejo and Cognac VSOP print with no description. Of 14 items, only the 4 cocktails are appetising.

Criterion 14: Brut Rosé $13 has no glass/bottle label, and it sits under SPARKLING, below the 'By the glass' label, so a guest will assume by the glass. No beer or spirit shows a pour size. The Brandy card is roughly 70% illustration around a single name-only line, which looks orphaned.

Criterion 10/13: the proposal lists Spanish pairs (De la casa, Clásicos, Brandy y coñac) that do not appear on the print. The name bars (EL VASO, LA COPA, LA COPITA) are good lotería voice, but the body copy switches between recipe-card terse ('Shaken; up, in a coupe.') and stub copy. Brandy placed ahead of Wine breaks the order a guest expects.

Criterion 13: the lotería deck fits a cantina well, and the $7-18 prices fit an Iowa City college-town tier. But the agave card holds only two tequilas, with no brand or mezcal, which is thin for a venue named Cantina.
fixes: Remove 'fresh' from the Margarita and Daiquiri, and print 'agave' and 'demerara' as the draft words (or cite a prep_recipes row for each syrup) so every ingredient word traces to a row.

Ask the venue for producer/region for the wines, brewery/ABV for the beers and brand/age for the Añejo and Cognac VSOP, and meanwhile write short guest-language lines only from those facts rather than printing category glosses.
Label the Brut Rosé price (glass or bottle) and add pour-size labels as soon as the venue supplies them. Until then, do not place Sparkling where it reads as part of 'By the glass'.

Either print the Spanish subheaders the proposal promises (De la casa, Clásicos, Brandy y coñac) or remove them from the proposal, and move Brandy after Wine (or fold it into the agave/spirits card) so the section order meets guest expectations.
Put the Manhattan 'aromatic bitters' back unless the venue confirms hiding it, because the draft menu_description (bf732e78) prints it.

lens: description quality and one guest voice
top_problem: The menu speaks in three different voices, and none of them is a guest voice. The cocktails read like prep sheets ('Shaken; up, in a coupe.', 'Stirred; over a large cube.'). The beer, cider and wine lines are three-word category labels that mostly repeat the item name ('Toasty amber lager.' under Amber Lager, 'Hop-forward draft IPA.' under Dry-Hopped IPA, 'Dry sparkling cider.' under Dry Cider, 'Dry red wine.' under Malbec). The spirits have either a trivia note ('Also called plata.') or no description at all (Añejo, Cognac VSOP). Only the Margarita line has any appetite in it ('Bright and citrus-forward'). Every fact traces to a source, but the copy doesn't sell anything and gives criterion 12's automatic fail (descriptions that repeat the name).
fixes: Rewrite the four cocktail lines in one guest voice: spirit and flavour first, then the verified garnish and glass as one light phrase (e.g. '...finished with an orange peel, over a large cube'). Drop the semicolon method stacks. Every noun should still trace to its recipe_versions / recipe_components row.

Replace the beer, cider and wine lines that repeat the name. Ask the venue (through the Coordinator) for brewery/producer, region and ABV, then write one sensory clause from those facts. Until the facts arrive, print nothing rather than a line that just restates the name.

Remove 'Also called plata.' It's taxonomy trivia, not appetising copy. Treat Blanco, Añejo and Cognac VSOP the same way (name only, with brand, age and pour flagged) so the spirits card uses one rule.

Layout note for the designer: Brut Rosé sits under Sparkling with no glass/bottle label (the draft label is empty), and there are no pour sizes for beer, spirits or wine. Get them from the venue and print them once in each subheader. Also, the 'LA BOTELLA' name bar sits on a card whose only list is 'By the Glass / Por copa', which contradicts itself. Retitle it or confirm bottle service.

Make the Spanish consistent: the proposal lists De la casa, Clásicos and Brandy y coñac, but the print shows only the English names on cards 2, 3 and 5, while Draft, Cider, Agave, By the Glass and Sparkling carry Spanish pairs. Also, EL VASO, LA COPA and EL AGAVE are not traditional Don Clemente lotería cards (LA BOTELLA is). Either call them house cards or use real card names.

The draft is written for a college town (median age 28.6, 29.9% aged 21-34, 47.6% with a bachelor's degree, median household income $52,960, 11% Hispanic/Latino; phg_census_zcta 52240), and in that setting the copy reads like a glossary, not a cantina.

lens: descriptions and prices laid out together in the print PNG (round-6/preview-letter.png, 2550x3300)
top_problem: The facts are sourced, but the prices sit on very uneven copy. The four cocktails get full three-line specs. Beer, cider and wine get three-word category lines ('Dry red wine.', 'Crisp pale lager.'). Añejo Tequila and Cognac VSOP are bare names with a price. So the right-hand price column reads as stuck onto a list, not as a menu that explains what each price buys. The worst case is the Brandy card: 69% of it is the figure, and it holds one line, 'Cognac VSOP 18', with no pour, house or description. No price in the menu has a pour or glass/bottle label, and Brut Rosé has no glass/bottle label at all. Verified sources (phg_designer_query log_id 125): Margarita rv f06abb74 (Rocks, Lime wheel, 'Shake with ice and strain over fresh ice'), Brown Butter Old Fashioned rv 7095fd3d (Rocks, Orange peel, 'Stir with ice and strain over a large cube'), House Daiquiri rv 14d45e57 (Coupe, Lime coin, 'Shake with ice and fine strain'), Manhattan rv 9fb77eaa (Coupe, Cocktail cherry, 'Stir with ice and strain'). All printed garnish, glass and method words trace to these rows. The beer, cider and wine lines match the menu_items.menu_description text word for word (ids 90b0a7e3, 8fb136cd, 70657e1e, 65c39a14, f6f9d57e, 5ba7511f, 32a35bd3). All 14 prices match menu_items.menu_price. 'Also called plata.' traces to beverage_categories 04d72e1f ('Blanco / plata'). No invented fact was found. Criterion 11 is held back only because 'Rye whiskey' widens the draft's 'Rye' (it is backed by the doc component 'Rye Whiskey') and because no brand, ABV, region or age exists for any spirit, beer or wine.
fixes: Get pour sizes (tequila and cognac oz, beer pint/oz, wine glass oz) and Brut Rosé glass-or-bottle through the Coordinator's needs_input. Print them as small labels next to the price (for example '5 oz  12'), because right now no price on the page says what it buys.

Designer: rebalance the Brandy card (69% figure, one name-only line) and Classics (55% figure, one item) so the cards hold items instead of empty art. For example, merge Brandy into the agave/spirits card or give Cognac VSOP a sourced line once the venue supplies a house. A lone 'Cognac VSOP 18' under a huge glass reads as an orphaned price.

Bring the description voice closer across cards. Keep the cocktails' 'ingredients; garnish. Method; serve.' pattern, and ask the venue for the brewery/ABV and producer/region rows so the beer and wine lines can grow past three generic words ('Dry red wine.' and 'Dry white wine.' read as category labels, not guest copy).

Designer: fix the Manhattan line break. It currently breaks 'Stirred; up, in / a coupe.', splitting the serve phrase. Tie 'up, in a coupe' together, or shorten the line to 'Stirred; served up.' (the coupe is sourced from rv 9fb77eaa).

Venue fit: 'CERVEZA Y SIDRA' breaks the lotería El/La single-noun name bars (EL AGAVE, EL VASO, LA COPA, LA COPITA, LA BOTELLA). Use a lotería-style singular such as 'EL BARRIL' to match the card's draft figure and the 'De barril' subheader. Also flag to the Coordinator that a cantina offering only two tequilas and no mezcal or non-alcoholic section feels thin for Iowa City guests (only in the draft's gift; do not invent items).

lens: descriptions and prices laid out together on the phone PNG
top_problem: On the phone, the prices are the least informative part of the menu. Brut Rosé 13 sits under 'Sparkling / Espumoso' with no glass or bottle label: the draft label is empty, and the Wine card only says 'By the glass' over Malbec and Pinot Grigio. Añejo 16 and Cognac VSOP 18 print as bare name + price lines with no description, pour size or age. Every beer and wine price is attached to a 3-4 word draft line ('Dry red wine.', 'Crisp pale lager.'). The large figures (the Brandy card's figure is 0.69 of its height, and the whole deck is a 9153 px scroll for 14 items) take far more space than the item copy, so the price-to-description relationship feels thin and unfinished rather than deliberate.

On the phone, prices at the same right edge no longer read as one column. The descriptions are 3-5 words next to a 40+ px serif price, so the price outweighs the copy.

Criterion 12: two voices. Cocktails are spec strings in bartender shorthand ('; lime wheel. ... Shaken; on the rocks.'). Beer and wine are near-taxonomy ('Dry red wine.', 'Dry white wine.', 'Dry sparkling rosé.'). 'Also called plata.' is a glossary note. None of it is guest language that sells.

Criterion 13: the cantina concept (lotería) is right for the venue, but the agave list is two generic tequilas with no mezcal and no brands. 'Del agave' is an awkward Spanish subheader ('Agaves' or 'Tequila y mezcal' is more natural). For a cantina, the agave card should be the deepest list, not the thinnest.

Criterion 11: every printed fact traces to a row, but 'Blanco tequila' reverses the source 'Tequila Blanco'. Brand, ABV, region, producer and pour size are missing everywhere, so the menu is accurate mostly because it says very little.
fixes: Get the Brut Rosé glass/bottle answer from the venue and print the pour label (for example 'glass 13') in the same small-caps label style as 'By the glass'; until then, drop it from the Sparkling heading rather than implying a glass pour.

Ask the venue for the Añejo and Cognac brands, age statements and pour sizes, and print them as a one-line description under each name (for example '[brand] · aged [n] months · 1.5 oz'); until they arrive, the designer should tighten those cards so the name + price lines are not stranded under huge figures.

Rewrite the cocktail lines as guest sentences built only from the cited recipe rows (for example 'Tequila blanco, fresh lime and orange liqueur, sweetened with agave; bright and citrus-forward, shaken and served over ice with a lime wheel'). Keep method words out of semicolon shorthand.
Match 'Tequila blanco' to the draft and component wording (menu_items 14555870 / recipe_versions f06abb74). Rename 'Del agave' to 'Agaves' and keep the Spanish subheaders as natural category nouns.

Layout note for the designer: remove the card tilt on the phone, or counter-rotate the price column so the prices share one right edge, and cut the figure height on one- and two-item cards so the descriptions and prices lead the scroll.
